description: We’re looking for teammates in UI/UX, game design, illustration. Join us to make space science engaging—curiosity and creativity welcome!
summary: Faraway Garden is a playful astronaut mission trainer for ages 7–12. Players run a Mars greenhouse, balancing limited power, water, food, life support and storm protection, then continue their training on the Moon. They grow crops, care for the crew, drive a rover, and learn through daily lessons, pet quizzes, science cards, badges and a training certificate. Historical NASA observations and research connect these choices to real space science. Storm effects, crop growth, resource costs and mission timing are clearly labeled simulations. By making engineering trade-offs tangible and giving players a reason to try again, the game turns space science into decisions young explorers can understand.
details:
Faraway Garden turns a space outpost into a sequence of choices a young explorer can understand. In its Mars greenhouse, players plant and water crops and divide six power cells among grow lights, heating, storm shelter and the rover battery. Those choices affect food, air and crew wellbeing. Players also explore with Bolt the rover, including manual 3D driving, and continue into a Moon training campaign. Rescue and retry encourage experimentation when a plan fails.

Daily lessons use See it, Try it, Say it activities. Pet quizzes, collectible Wiz Cards, badges, a mission journal and a training certificate connect play to reflection. The intended benefit is to help children practice resource planning and explain why life support, power, radiation protection and food production compete. Educational impact has not yet been measured; classroom playtesting is a future step.

NASA data supplies the scientific context: historical DONKI solar-event records from May 2024; archived InSight weather from October 2020; NASA plant research; a date-specific JPL Horizons Earth–Mars light-time estimate; credited NASA rover photographs; and Mars Trek terrain imagery. Source-backed science cards connect these resources to activities. The observations retain their original context: storm strength, timing and Mars-outpost effects, crop growth and yields, driving costs and compressed communication time are game simulations. Earth geomagnetic records are not evidence of a Mars impact. Archived records are not live feeds.

Built with Phaser 3, TypeScript and Vite, the browser game stores progress locally when available. A first load needs a network connection; offline operation is not promised. Project pixel art is drawn in code. Claude and OpenAI Codex assisted with brainstorming, implementation, dialogue, science summaries, validation, documentation and the presentation. The seven-slide demo contains staged game screenshots, not evidence of completed missions or measured learning outcomes. Background music was generated with Suno and provided by Muskan; sound effects use Kenney assets. Detailed tool, asset, data and license credits are available in the repository.
